From the owner
The most common mistake we see in kitchen design is treating everything as equally permanent. Some decisions in a kitchen should be built to last decades. Others can and should reflect how you actually live right now. The structural decisions, layout, cabinetry quality, countertop material, lighting infrastructure, are the ones worth spending on. These are difficult and expensive to change later, and they set the ceiling for everything else in the space. The finish decisions, cabinet color, hardware, backsplash tile, paint, are the ones with more flexibility. These are the places where personal style belongs, because they can be updated as tastes evolve without rebuilding the kitchen. The kitchens that hold up best over time are the ones where this thinking was applied from the start. A well-proportioned layout with quality cabinetry and stone countertops in a color that ages quickly still has good bones. A trendy layout with cheap cabinetry does not. A few things we consistently recommend building to last: solid wood or plywood box cabinetry, stone or quartz countertops, hardwired under-cabinet lighting and a layout that fits how the household actually moves through the space. A few things where personal style belongs: cabinet color, cabinet hardware, backsplash pattern and paint color. We go deeper on this in our full guide at atlasdesignandbuild.com. Reach out through our profile to talk through your kitchen.

Our Heirloom Kitchen Renovation Project in Middle TN is completed, and we're excited to begin showing this renovation off! Every inch of our Heirloom Kitchen Project was intentionally designed around how this homeowner cooks, stores, collects, and lives. We incorporated design elements she had collected over time, along with materials she already knew and loved, including soapstone and unlacquered brass that will continue to develop character as they age. From smart corner storage and lighted cabinetry to a pantry that keeps everything organized, each detail has a purpose. Even the X detailing on the cabinetry is a subtle nod to the homeowners’ equestrian lifestyle. Because the best kitchens aren’t just beautiful. They feel deeply personal and work beautifully, too. ADU zoning rules in San Carlos CA — what state law actually allows in 2026. California has removed most local barriers to ADU construction. Here's what matters for your property: What you're entitled to build: – 1 ADU (attached, detached, or garage conversion) – 1 Junior ADU within the existing structure (up to 500 sq ft) – In many cases: both an ADU and a JADU on the same lot simultaneously What San Carlos cannot require from you: –Replacement parking for a garage conversion — Owner-occupancy (for ADUs permitted after Jan 1, 2020) — Discretionary design review for most ADU applications The setback exemption most homeowners miss: If your garage was legally built close to the property line, it can typically still be converted to an ADU — even if it doesn't meet standard new construction setbacks. This opens eligibility to many San Carlos properties homeowners assume don't qualify. In 2023, San Mateo County permitted 600+ ADUs — driven directly by these state preemption laws. Brian Pezzulich (CA License #957500) visits your property, checks zoning and setbacks, and tells you exactly what's possible before any fees are committed. Why can two cabinet-refacing estimates be thousands of dollars apart? It's a question I hear from homeowners all the time. A higher price doesn't automatically mean you're getting better doors, hardware, or craftsmanship. Kitchen Transformations is an independent, local cabinet-refacing company with a low-overhead business model. We don't have franchise royalties, layers of corporate management, or a commissioned in-home sales force built into our pricing. That's how we can focus your money where it matters: premium-quality materials, experienced installation, and the finished kitchen. We've seen just how significant the difference can be. On one Greater Cincinnati project, the homeowner had received a $25,000 cabinet-refacing estimate. Kitchen Transformations completed a comparable project scope for $13,700 — an $11,300 difference. Our philosophy is simple: Premium-quality cabinet refacing without the corporate overhead. If you've already received a cabinet-refacing estimate and the price surprised you, get one more price before making your decision. We also built the stairs and railing into the project so everything works together instead of looking pieced together later. A good deck build isn’t just about making the finished boards look nice. From the owner
Planning a remodel? Knowing the stages and timeline helps you avoid surprises and make confident decisions. At Newrome, we guide homeowners through home remodeling in Miami with clear planning, quality craftsmanship, and code-compliant construction. A typical whole home remodel starts with an in-home consultation and design review, then moves into budgeting, selections, Miami-Dade permitting, demolition, rough plumbing/electrical, framing, inspections, finishes, and final walkthrough. Smaller interior renovation projects may take 4–8 weeks, while larger Miami home remodeling projects can take 3–6+ months depending on scope, materials, and approvals. Because South Florida homes face humidity, storms, and strict building requirements, our licensed and insured team focuses on durability, Florida Building Code compliance, and smart upgrades that improve comfort and resale value. From Coral Gables and Coconut Grove to Brickell, Pinecrest, and Key Biscayne, we understand local homes and permitting needs. If you’re searching for home remodeling Miami, home remodeling Miami FL, or home remodeling contractors Miami near me, Newrome is ready to help you plan the right timeline from day one. Schedule your free consultation or in-home estimate today and start your renovation with a trusted Miami renovation team.

From the owner
Fall deck check before the first freeze in DuPage County Gray boards are weathering. Soft wood is not. Before frost sets in, it pays to know which one your deck has. A deck gets judged by its boards, but the frame underneath decides repair or rebuild. The ledger fixed to the house carries roughly half the load. Joist tops rot first, hidden under the decking. Footings move with frost, and a corner that has dropped is the warning sign. Three checks worth doing this weekend: • Push a screwdriver into the joists, post bases and stair stringers. Sound wood stops it. • Look at the ledger. Bolt heads are good. Nail heads alone are not. • Look for rust streaks running below the fasteners. Board replacement over a sound frame starts at $10 per sq ft. A typical 200 sq ft re-deck starts at $1,995. Perfect Work Remodeling & Repairs lifts boards before quoting, so the written scope covers the frame, not just the surface. Free deck inspection with a repair estimate in Carol Stream, Wheaton, Glen Ellyn, Winfield, Naperville and Hinsdale.
